+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|            PLATFORM CAPITALISM LANDSCAPE                         |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  PLATFORM TYPES (Srnicek)                                        |
|  Advertising: Google, Meta (sell user attention)                 |
|  Cloud: AWS, Azure, GCP (sell computing infrastructure)          |
|  Product: Amazon, Apple App Store (sell products + ecosystem)    |
|  Lean: Uber, Airbnb (asset-light, extract from providers)        |
|  Industrial: Siemens, GE (B2B data extraction)                   |
|                                                                  |
|  SURVEILLANCE CAPITALISM (Zuboff)                                |
|  Behavioral data extraction --> prediction products              |
|  --> behavioral modification --> sold to advertisers             |
|                                                                  |
|  ATTENTION ECONOMY                                               |
|  Herbert Simon: attention is the scarce resource                 |
|  Engagement optimization: maximize time-on-platform             |
|  Outrage, anxiety, and controversy are more engaging            |
|  Variable reward schedules: slot machine dynamics               |
|                                                                  |
|  NETWORK EFFECTS                                                 |
|  Winner-take-all dynamics in platform markets                   |
|  Direct network effects (Facebook: more users = more value)     |
|  Indirect effects (App Store: more apps = more users)           |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

PLATFORM = DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE THAT ENABLES
             TWO OR MORE GROUPS TO INTERACT

  Core economic logic:
  - Platforms position themselves as intermediaries
  - Extract rent from interactions they facilitate
  - Value = data generated by interactions
  - Network effects create monopoly dynamics

  MULTISIDED MARKET:
  +-----------+                +-----------+
  |  GROUP A  | <-- Platform   |  GROUP B  |
  |  (Users)  |   mediates     |Advertisers|
  |           |   interaction  | Sellers,  |
  |           |                | Developers|
  +-----------+                +-----------+

  Google mediates users and advertisers.
  iPhone mediates users and app developers.
  Uber mediates riders and drivers.
  Amazon mediates buyers and sellers.

  Platform captures data from interactions.
  Data improves platform.
  Better platform attracts more users.
  More users generate more data.
  Feedback loop --> monopoly.

+------------------+------------------------------------------+---------------+
| TYPE             | DESCRIPTION                              | EXAMPLES      |
+------------------+------------------------------------------+---------------+
| ADVERTISING      | Free service to users; sell user          | Google, Meta,  |
|                  | attention/data to advertisers            | YouTube, TikTok|
+------------------+------------------------------------------+---------------+
| CLOUD            | Sell computing resources and services    | AWS, Azure,   |
|                  | to businesses; near-commodity pricing    | GCP           |
+------------------+------------------------------------------+---------------+
| INDUSTRIAL       | Sensors + data analytics for             | GE Predix,     |
|                  | manufacturers/infrastructure             | Siemens MindS. |
+------------------+------------------------------------------+---------------+
| PRODUCT          | Leverage platform position to sell       | Apple hardware|
|                  | products + ecosystem lock-in             | Amazon retail |
+------------------+------------------------------------------+---------------+
| LEAN             | Outsource assets to providers;           | Uber, Airbnb,  |
|                  | extract fee from transactions            | TaskRabbit     |
+------------------+------------------------------------------+---------------+

SURVEILLANCE CAPITALISM CYCLE
  ==============================

  STEP 1: BEHAVIORAL DATA EXTRACTION
    Users interact with platform (search, click, scroll,
    post, message, purchase, GPS location, facial expression
    in video)
    Platform captures ALL behavioral data
    (most never requested by user; "behavioral exhaust")

  STEP 2: BEHAVIORAL DATA PROCESSING
    Raw data --> prediction product
    Not just demographic targeting
    But: modeling future behavior
    "At 2pm on a Tuesday when you are slightly stressed,
     you are 78% more likely to click this kind of ad"

  STEP 3: BEHAVIORAL MODIFICATION
    Platforms sell not just predictions but INTERVENTIONS.
    Not: "Here is a user likely to buy shoes"
    But: "We can MAKE this user likely to buy shoes"
    (nudging, recommendations, notification timing)

  STEP 4: INSTRUMENTATION OF POWER
    Platforms that can predict and modify behavior
    at scale have political power.
    Facebook "I Voted" study (2012): showed voting
    badge to 61 million users --> 340,000 additional votes.
    This is behavior modification at civic scale.

  ZUBOFF'S ARGUMENT:
    This is not just privacy violation.
    It is a new form of power over human behavior.
    "Instrumentarian power": behavior modification
    without violence, without ideology, through
    continuous environmental design.

NETWORK EFFECTS: WHY PLATFORMS MONOPOLIZE
  ==========================================

  DIRECT NETWORK EFFECT (Metcalfe's Law):
    Value scales as n(n-1)/2 — the number of possible
    connections in an n-node network. This is why
    network effects are superlinear: doubling users
    roughly quadruples connection value.
    Telephone: useless with one user;
               valuable with everyone you know on it.
    Facebook: boring with 10 friends;
              irreplaceable with 500.

  INDIRECT NETWORK EFFECT:
    Product becomes more valuable as more complementors
    join the other side.
    iOS App Store: more apps = more valuable to users.
    More users = more attractive to app developers.

  WINNER-TAKE-ALL DYNAMICS:
    In network-effect markets, the leading platform
    tends to take all (or most) of the market.
    Why would you use the second-best social network
    if all your friends are on the best one?

    Platform Market Structure:
    - Search: Google ~92% global share
    - Social: Facebook/Instagram/WhatsApp ~60% global social graph
    - Mobile OS: Android + iOS = ~99%
    - Cloud: AWS + Azure + GCP = ~65%
    - E-commerce US: Amazon ~40% of all online sales

  DATA NETWORK EFFECTS (additional moat):
    More users = more data = better algorithm = more users.
    Data creates additional winner-take-all dynamic
    beyond traditional network effects.

blocks.heading_context: ## Engineering Bridge: Platform Mechanics in Cloud and Enterprise
blocks.text:
PLATFORM CAPITALISM CONCEPT    ENGINEERING / CLOUD PARALLEL
===========================    ============================

Multisided market              Azure Marketplace: Microsoft mediates
(platform mediates two groups) ISV software vendors (one side) and
                               Azure enterprise customers (other side).
                               Microsoft extracts transaction fees (20%)
                               from vendor sales while providing access
                               to enterprise customer base. Identical
                               structural logic to Uber (driver/rider)
                               and Google (advertiser/user).

Rent extraction from           Cloud pricing models: AWS/Azure/GCP
platform position              charge per-unit consumption (compute,
                               storage, egress) on top of open-source
                               software you could run yourself. The
                               rent is the convenience + integration +
                               managed service wrapper. Srnicek's
                               "lean platform" model applied: the
                               cloud provider owns the infrastructure
                               and extracts rent from usage while
                               providers (cloud customers) bear the
                               build cost of their applications.

Data moats and network effects Azure telemetry: every interaction with
(data network effects)         Azure services generates usage data that
                               improves recommendations, security alerts,
                               capacity planning, and ML model training.
                               More Azure customers → more telemetry →
                               better service → more customers. Data
                               network effect operating at infrastructure
                               level — exact same mechanism as Google
                               Search improving with query volume.

Winner-take-all cloud market   AWS + Azure + GCP = ~65% of cloud market.
                               Classic winner-take-all with indirect
                               network effects: more services on platform
                               → more developer familiarity → more
                               enterprise adoption → more ISV investment
                               → more services. Each layer strengthens
                               the others. Same flywheel as App Store.

Vendor lock-in as moat         Proprietary data formats, closed APIs,
                               and switching costs create the same
                               structural dependency as social network
                               lock-in. Azure AD, ADF pipelines,
                               Power Platform integrations — each
                               additional integration raises the
                               switching cost to competitors.
                               This is Srnicek's "data extraction"
                               logic applied to enterprise software.
